stories.headline: Iran steps up Gulf attacks as US blockade bites
body: At least 25 tankers have been hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz in the past week.
Iran also claims to have targeted US radars in Bahrain and downed US drones.
Iran's president calls the US blockade and sanctions a 'silent economic war'.
stories.vc: Gulf oil flows have dropped sharply, pushing up energy risk worldwide.

stories.headline: Suspected drone strike hits Russian warship in Libya's Benghazi
body: A suspected sea-drone attack hit a Russian vessel in Benghazi port, Libya's eastern government says.
Local sources say Libyan and Russian nationals were killed and the ship carried weapons.
Satellite images suggest it was the Russian corvette Merkury.
stories.vc: The war's spread to Africa adds risk to Mediterranean shipping.

stories.statLabel: people arrested on a jet bridge
stories.headline: Officials condemn ICE arrests at Seattle airport
body: Masked immigration agents detained two people on a Seattle airport jet bridge as passengers boarded.
A video of the arrests went viral.
Democratic leaders called the tactics 'atrocious' and want limits on ICE.
stories.vc: Airport enforcement raises concerns for travel and tourism.

stories.headline: Bengaluru's Swish grows revenue 10x, but losses nearly quadruple
body: Quick food delivery startup Swish made ₹47.6 crore in operating revenue in FY26, over 10 times the year before.
Its loss rose nearly 4x to ₹91.1 crore.
Expenses jumped more than 5x to ₹144.8 crore.
stories.joke: Ten-minute food, ten-times growth, ten-tonne losses.
stories.vc: Quick-food startups are burning cash fast to win customers.

stories.headline: VinFast to build e-scooters at its Tamil Nadu plant
body: Vietnam's VinFast is building an electric scooter line at its Thoothukudi plant in Tamil Nadu.
It signed for 500 more acres of land with the state last year.
The first scooters should roll out early next year.
stories.joke: Thoothukudi, now with fewer petrol fumes.
stories.vc: More EV plants bring jobs and investment to southern Tamil Nadu.

stories.headline: FSSAI orders prosecution of Bisleri over unsafe water sample
body: Food regulator FSSAI has approved prosecution of Bisleri International.
A packaged drinking water sample failed limits for bromate, a chemical, and was declared unsafe.
The sample was taken from Bisleri's own premises.
stories.joke: Even water needs a background check now.
stories.vc: Safety action can hit trust in big consumer brands.

stories.headline: Why data centres are the centre of the Big Tech backlash
body: Journalist Paris Marx's book 'Hyperscale' looks inside data centres and the AI boom.
He calls the build-out 'fundamentally unsustainable'.
Data-centre anger may have helped drive the midterm blue wave. (No new FT/Unhedged piece, so this is TechCrunch's interview.)
stories.joke: The cloud has a very real electricity bill.
stories.vc: Local pushback could slow and raise the cost of AI infrastructure.

stories.statLabel: Tesla vs Waymo robotaxis in Texas
stories.headline: Tesla now has more robotaxis registered in Texas than Waymo
body: Tesla has 1,507 robotaxis registered in Texas, ahead of Waymo's 1,345.
Waymo has pulled robotaxis off freeways again, while Zoox launched on Uber.
TechCrunch says paid rides matter more than registrations. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: Counting cars is easy; counting riders is the test.
stories.vc: The robotaxi race will be won on revenue, not fleet size.

stories.statLabel: TDS and tax on crypto gains
stories.headline: Crypto industry asks for tax relief in Budget 2027
body: The Bharat Web3 Association wants the government to rethink the 1% TDS and 30% tax on crypto profits.
It says clear rules would give compliant Indian platforms certainty.
Exchanges face bank problems, hacks and scrutiny. (TechCrunch Venture had no fresh deal, so this is Inc42's report.)
stories.vc: Lower taxes could bring trading back to Indian exchanges.

stories.headline: OpenAI's chief scientist floats ways to limit AI development
body: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki wrote about possible limits on AI development.
He focuses on 'perplexity', a measure of how well a model predicts text.
Anthropic's Dario Amodei has proposed a plan to 'pace the frontier'. (No new Stratechery post, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.vc: Industry-agreed limits could slow the AI spending race.

stories.headline: Theranos documentary 'You Can See Everything' tops $100M
body: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's Elizabeth Holmes documentary has made $102.4 million worldwide.
Almost all of it came from the US; reported budget was $7 million.
It opens in Mexico, Brazil and Argentina next week. (No checkable Economist piece, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: The blood test failed; the movie didn't.
stories.vc: Indie studio A24 shows documentaries can be big business.

stories.headline: NCW chief calls for equal respect and support for single women
body: NCW chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar says society must support women whatever their marital status.
She called for economic independence, secure housing, social security and legal help for single women.
She spoke at a national consultation in New Delhi.
stories.vc: Secure housing and jobs help single women stay financially independent.

stories.headline: Aber Kawas becomes first Palestinian in New York's state Senate
body: Aber Kawas, 34, won a New York state Senate seat with 74.5% of the vote.
She is the first Palestinian and first Muslim woman in New York's state legislature.
She represents a Queens district where nearly half the residents were born abroad.
stories.joke: History made, in a tatreez blazer.
stories.vc: Diverse representation can shift local budget priorities.

stories.headline: Kansas City Current win the NWSL title over Washington Spirit
body: Kansas City Current beat Washington Spirit 2–1 to win the women's NWSL championship.
The Spirit lost their third final in a row, in front of a sold-out home crowd.
Star Trinity Rodman played through a shoulder injury.
stories.vc: Sold-out women's finals show the league's growing commercial pull.

stories.headline: Karnataka approves a 100-bed Jayadeva heart centre in west Bengaluru
body: Karnataka's cabinet approved leasing a 100-bed government hospital in Govindarajanagar to Jayadeva.
It will become a dedicated cardiac care centre for west Bengaluru.
Patients there now travel nearly an hour to Jayadeva on Bannerghatta Road.
stories.vc: A satellite centre spreads specialist care across the city.

stories.headline: Punjab to open 333 new village clinics
body: Punjab will open 333 new Pind Clinics, taking the total to 591.
These village clinics bring basic healthcare closer to home.
They add to 1,244 Aam Aadmi Clinics in cities.
stories.vc: Primary care close to home cuts pressure on big hospitals.

stories.headline: Indore's MY Hospital to open a yellow fever vaccine centre
body: Maharaja Yeshwantrao Hospital in Indore will start yellow fever vaccinations from November 27.
Travellers now have to go to Bhopal for the vaccine.
MGM Medical College got central approval for the centre.
stories.joke: Passport, ticket, jab: now all local.
stories.vc: Local vaccine centres make international travel easier.

stories.headline: Liquidnet's US algo chief Vinisha Minocha joins TD Securities
body: Vinisha Minocha has joined TD Securities in New York as a director in electronic trading.
She spent over eight years as Liquidnet's US head of algos coverage.
She began her career in 1998 in proprietary trading at JP Morgan.
stories.vc: Banks keep competing for electronic trading talent.

stories.headline: Kepler Cheuvreux and Centile launch a derivatives broker
body: Kepler Cheuvreux and Centile Partners have launched Kepler Centile, a derivatives brokerage.
It offers agency execution, trade ideas and market insight in listed derivatives and FX.
Clients can trade futures and options on major global exchanges.
stories.vc: More independent brokers give funds choice beyond big banks.

stories.headline: Explainer: What's the difference between a broker and a prop trader?
body: Imagine asking a friend to buy sweets for you at the shop. They use your money and bring back your sweets.
That friend is like a broker. Grown-ups call this agency trading.
A prop trader is different: they buy and sell with their own money, hoping to profit.
This week, Kepler Centile launched to do agency trading in futures and options for clients.
Knowing who you deal with matters: a broker works for you; a prop trader works for themselves.
stories.vc: Clear roles protect investors.

stories.headline: Verstappen wins a wild Las Vegas GP with 35 lead changes
body: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix by 0.639 seconds from Lando Norris, with Oscar Piastri third.
The race had 35 lead changes in 50 laps as cars slipstreamed nose to tail.
George Russell hit the barriers late and finished ninth.
stories.joke: Vegas: where even the lead changes hands constantly.
stories.vc: A thriller like this is gold for F1's US TV audience and sponsors.
